newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Khmer Rouge leader backs Cambodia constitution.
newsitem.headline: Khmer Rouge leader backs Cambodia constitution.

text.p: Khmer Rouge front man Khieu Samphan said on the guerrillas' clandestine radio on Sunday that he supported the Cambodian constitution and the reviled rebel leader Pol Pot was politically finished.
"The regime and organisation of Pol Pot has ended," Khieu Samphan said in the broadcast monitored in Phnom Penh.
Khieu Samphan, the guerrilla group's main political leader, said his National Solidarity Party recognised and would defend the constitution.
Khieu Samphan and other top Khmer Rouge figures broke with Pol Pot in May after a violent falling out among the group's top leaders.

The radio announcement came as fighting between forces loyal to the country's rival prime ministers continued in the capital. The fighting began on Saturday after Second Prime Minister Hun Sen said his forces had to take action against defectors from the Khmer Rouge smuggled into the capital by his co-premier.

First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh denied bringing Khmer Rouge into the city, although he has been negotiating with the rebels and hinted he would be willing to form a political alliance with Khieu Samphan. He said on Saturday he had become head of Cambodia's only legitimate government as a result of Hun Sen's alleged coup attempt.
